q: Under RA 9514, what minimum width must a fire exit stair have?
n: 60 cm, wider than either 1977 Fire Code type: 55.9 cm for the EX stair and 45.7 cm for the EX-SB.

q: Under PD 1096, how far must a firewall extend horizontally past the wall it protects?
n: 600 mm horizontally, and 400 mm above the roof, so fire cannot lap around or over it.

q: At what height above the floor should a door pull handle be set?
n: Pull handles sit at 1.06 m, the same height used for guards, so a standing adult reaches both without stooping.

q: What maximum vertical spacing applies between balusters on a fire exit stair?
n: 15.25 cm, close enough that a small child cannot pass between them.

q: Under PD 1096, what is the maximum slope of an exit passageway?
n: An exit passageway may slope up to 1:8. An exit court is stricter at 1:10. Easy to swap: the court is outdoors and carries more people, so it stays flatter.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what maximum rise applied to the EX-SB stair, whose treads are flat metal bars?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 30.5 cm, far steeper than the 22.9 cm allowed on the EX stair. The EX-SB was the lighter escape type.

q: What minimum rear setback applies to an R-1 lot?
n: R-1 runs 4.50 m front, 2.00 m sides, 2.00 m rear.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum stair width serves an occupant load of 10 to 50?
n: Three bands: 750 mm below 10, 900 mm up to 50, 1100 mm above 50. Handrails may eat 100 mm of that width, no more.

q: Under RA 9514, what tread depth must a winder give 305 mm from its narrowest edge?
n: 280 mm at that point, and never less than 150 mm anywhere along the tread.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, at the steepest allowed slope (1:15), a ramp needs a landing at least every how many meters?
n: At 1:15 a landing is needed every 10 m; at 1:20, every 15 m. The 1994 IRR required one every 6.00 m at 1:12.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what minimum nosing projection applied to the EX stair, whose treads are solid with 13 mm perforations?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 2.5 cm on the EX stair. The EX-SB had no nosing requirement, since its treads were open metal bars.

q: What basic front setback applies to an R-3 lot?
n: R-3 starts at 3.00 m and may reach 8.00 m, the extra 5.00 m taken at grade for parking.

q: Under RA 9514, what maximum riser height applies to an existing stair?
n: Existing stairs may keep 205 mm risers and 230 mm treads. A new stair is held to 180 mm and 280 mm.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what width was required of a Class A ramp?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 122 cm for Class A. Class B ran 76 cm to 122 cm.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what tread construction was specified for the EX-SB fire exit stair?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: Flat metal bars, an open grating. The EX stair instead used solid treads with 13 mm perforations.

q: Under RA 9514, what minimum headroom must a fire exit stair have?
n: 2.00 m, between the 2.13 m of the 1977 EX stair and the 1.98 m of the EX-SB.

q: Under BP 220, what side setback applies to economic and socialized housing?
n: 1.50 m front and sides, 2.00 m rear, tighter than the PD 1096 residential figures.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum headroom must a stairway have?
n: 2000 mm, measured from a plane tangent to the tread nosings up to the soffit above.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, at what slope did a Class B ramp begin?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: Class B ran 8% to 17%. Anything gentler than 8% counted as Class A.

q: Under RA 9514, what minimum height applies to a main door?
n: 2000 mm high by 915 mm wide, matching the 915 mm minimum width of an existing stair.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, how could the EX-SB stair, whose treads are flat metal bars discharge to the ground?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: By a swinging stair section or a ladder. The heavier EX stair had only the swinging section.

q: What clearance applies between buildings of 3 to 4 storeys?
n: 6.0 m between the buildings, 2.0 m to the property line. It widens with height: 4.0 m and 1.50 m at 1 to 2 storeys, 10.0 m and 6.0 m above 4.

q: Under RA 9514, what is the maximum vertical height between stair landings?
n: 3660 mm, for both new and existing stairs. PD 1096 sets a slightly tighter 3.60 m.

q: Under RA 9514, what is the maximum rise for a single ramp run?
n: 760 mm. Past that the ramp needs a landing before it continues.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum width applies to a service door?
n: 700 mm, the same as a bedroom door. Only the main door needs 800 mm.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, how many persons per unit could escape through a window on an EX-SB stair?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 5 persons per unit through a window, against 38 through winders or a ladder from a balcony.

q: Under RA 9514, what sidewalk width range applies?
n: 0.60 m to 1.00 m. BP 344 is firmer, requiring 1.20 m kept clear.

q: Under BP 220, how long must a stair landing be in the direction of travel?
n: Equal to the width of the stairway, the same rule PD 1096 uses.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what capacity did a Class A ramp carry travelling up?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 45 going up, 60 going down. Descending is faster, so a ramp carries more that way.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum height applies to a bathroom door?
n: 1800 mm for bathroom and mezzanine doors, 2000 mm for every other door.

q: What minimum guard height applies at an interior balcony or mezzanine?
n: 91 cm at interior balconies and mezzanines, against 106 cm elsewhere.

q: Under PD 957, what planting strip width range applies?
n: 0.40 m to 1.30 m, the same band BP 220 uses.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what horizontal landing dimension applied to the EX stair, whose treads are solid with 13 mm perforations?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 55.9 cm, matching its own stair width.

q: Under BP 220, how far must a firewall extend above the roof?
n: 300 mm, against 400 mm under PD 1096.

q: What lower and upper dimension bracket a door kick plate?
n: A kick plate runs 0.30 m to 0.40 m up from the bottom of the door, where a wheelchair footrest strikes it.

q: Under BP 344, what clearance must a handrail keep from a ledge?
n: 40 mm from a ledge, against 50 mm from a wall, so a hand can close around the rail.

q: Under RA 9514, what is the maximum slope of an accessible ramp?
n: 1:12 maximum with a 1:48 cross slope. BP 344 is now stricter at 1:20 standard and 1:15 at worst.

q: Under RA 9514, what maximum rise applies to a fire exit stair?
n: 23 cm rise with a 23 cm tread, a steeper pairing than an ordinary stair.

q: What basic front setback applies to an R-2 lot?
n: R-2 starts at 3.00 m and may reach 6.00 m. R-3 is the one that reaches 8.00 m.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum stair width serves an occupant load above 50?
n: 1100 mm. Below 50 it drops to 900 mm, and a private stair under 10 occupants may be 750 mm.

q: Under BP 344, what minimum tread width applies at the narrow edge of a winder?
n: 150 mm at the narrow edge, rising to 200 mm measured 300 mm in.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what minimum length must an intermediate ramp landing have?
n: Intermediate landings are at least 1800 mm long. The 1994 IRR asked for 1.50 m.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what maximum height between landings applied to the EX stair, whose treads are solid with 13 mm perforations?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 3.66 m, the same figure RA 9514 carries today. The EX-SB had no requirement.

q: What maximum front setback applies to an R-3 lot?
n: 8.00 m: 3.00 m basic plus 5.00 m taken at grade for parking. Upper floors return to the 3.00 m line.

q: Under RA 9514, what minimum tread depth applies to a new stair?
n: 280 mm tread with a 180 mm maximum riser. An existing stair may stay at 230 mm and 205 mm.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what width range applied to a Class B ramp?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 76 cm to 122 cm. A Class A ramp was a flat 122 cm.

q: Under RA 9514, how is fire exit stair tread construction specified?
n: Solid, with 13 mm diameter perforations, so the tread drains but stays a continuous surface.

q: What minimum size must a door or casement window have to serve as fire exit access?
n: 61 cm by 1.98 m for a door or casement. A double-hung window needs 76.20 cm by 91.44 cm.

q: Under BP 220, what rear setback applies to economic and socialized housing?
n: 2.00 m rear, with 1.50 m at the front and sides.

q: Under RA 9514, what minimum headroom must a stair have?
n: 2000 mm, the same figure PD 1096 uses.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, at what slope did a Class B ramp stop being allowed?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 17%, the steepest Class B. Below 8% it is Class A instead.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum width applies to a main door?
n: 800 mm for the main door, 700 mm for bedroom and service doors, 600 mm for a bathroom door.

q: How many persons per unit may a fire exit stair serve through a door?
n: 45 persons per unit through a door, 20 through a window.

q: What clearance applies between buildings of more than 4 storeys?
n: 10.0 m between buildings and 6.0 m to the property line, the widest band.

q: Under BP 220, what is the maximum vertical height between stair landings?
n: 3.60 m, matching PD 1096.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what maximum rise applied to a single Class A ramp run?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: None. Class A had no limit, while Class B stopped at 3.66 m.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum height applies to a service door?
n: 2000 mm, like every door except bathroom and mezzanine doors at 1800 mm.

q: Under PD 1096, at what height above the nosing must a stair handrail be set?
n: 800 mm to 900 mm above the nosing. RA 9514 sits a little lower at 760 mm to 865 mm.

q: Under PD 957, what sidewalk width range applies to open market subdivisions?
n: 0.60 m to 1.20 m for open market, against 0.50 m to 1.20 m under BP 220.

q: Within one flight, how much may riser heights and tread widths vary?
n: 5 mm. Beyond that the stair reads as uneven underfoot and becomes a trip hazard.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what capacity did a Class B ramp carry travelling up?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 45 either way for Class B. Class A carried 45 up but 60 down.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum height applies to a mezzanine door?
n: 1800 mm, the same allowance given to a bathroom door.

q: Under PD 1096, from what floor level up must a building have a stairway reaching the roof?
n: Every building of four or more storeys needs one stairway extending to the roof, unless the roof is steeper than 1 in 3. The 50 mm handrail-to-wall clearance often paired with this is a BP 344 rule, not a PD 1096 one.

q: Under BP 220, what planting strip width range applies?
n: 0.40 m to 1.30 m, the same as PD 957.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what horizontal landing dimension applied to the EX-SB stair, whose treads are flat metal bars?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 45.7 cm, matching its own stair width.

q: Under BP 220, how far must a firewall extend horizontally past the wall it protects?
n: 300 mm horizontally and 300 mm above the roof, with a 150 mm wall thickness.

q: What minimum window opening must a habitable room have?
n: 10% of the floor area. Half of that, 5%, must be openable for ventilation.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum tread width is allowed at the narrow edge of a winder?
n: 150 mm at any point, with the full 250 mm run required 300 mm in from the narrow side.

q: Under RA 9514, what is the maximum cross slope of a ramp?
n: 1:48. The running slope may reach 1:12.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what minimum tread depth applied to the EX stair, whose treads are solid with 13 mm perforations?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 22.9 cm, excluding the nosing projection.

q: What is the maximum front setback for an R-2 building?
n: R-2 runs 3.00 m basic to 6.00 m maximum. R-3 is the one that reaches 8.00 m, made up of 3.00 m plus 5.00 m at grade for parking.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what total did two risers plus one tread have to fall within?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 60.00 cm to 63.50 cm, nosing projections excluded. It is the old rule of thumb that ties riser height to tread depth.

q: Under BP 344, what tread width must a winder give 300 mm from its narrowest edge?
n: 200 mm at that point, and never less than 150 mm at the narrow edge itself.

q: Under RA 9514, what minimum width must a ramp have?
n: 1120 mm, with landings of the same dimension.

q: Under RA 9514, what maximum height is allowed between fire exit stair landings?
n: 3.66 m, carried over unchanged from the 1977 EX stair.

q: What side setback applies to an R-3 lot?
n: 2.00 m on each side, the same as R-1 and R-2.

q: Under RA 9514, what minimum tread depth applies to an existing stair?
n: 230 mm, against 280 mm for a new stair.

q: Under RA 9514, what minimum ramp width applies?
n: 1120 mm, wider than the 1.20 m BP 344 asks of an accessible ramp only by a hair.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum width must a main door have?
n: 900 mm wide by 2000 mm high, the same leaf size required of an exit door.

q: What minimum size must a double-hung window have to serve as fire exit access?
n: 76.20 cm by 91.44 cm. A door or casement opening may be 61 cm by 1.98 m.

q: Under PD 957, what sets the required setbacks in a subdivision?
n: PD 957 sets none of its own. Setbacks follow PD 1096, the National Building Code.

q: Under PD 1096, what is the maximum vertical height between stair landings?
n: 3.60 m. Any taller run needs a landing to break the fall.

q: Under RA 9514, what is the steepest accessible ramp slope allowed?
n: 1:12. BP 344 now demands 1:20 as standard, with 1:15 only in special cases.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum height applies to a main door?
n: 2000 mm, with an 800 mm minimum width.

q: How many persons per unit may a fire exit stair serve through a window?
n: 20 persons per unit through a window, against 45 through a door.

q: What clearance applies where a wall is blank, with no openings?
n: 2.0 m between buildings and 1.0 m to the property line. A wall with openings needs more.

q: Under PD 1096, how long must a stair landing be in the direction of travel?
n: Equal to the stairway width, and it need not exceed 1.20 m where the stair runs straight.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what maximum rise applied to a single Class B ramp run?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 3.66 m for Class B. Class A had no limit at all.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum width applies to a bedroom door?
n: 700 mm, the same as a service door.

q: Under RA 9514, at what height above the tread surface must a handrail be set?
n: 760 mm to 865 mm above the tread. PD 1096 sits higher at 800 mm to 900 mm.

q: Under BP 220, what sidewalk width range applies to economic and socialized housing?
n: 0.50 m to 1.20 m, slightly narrower at the low end than the PD 957 open market range.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what minimum width applied to the EX stair, whose treads are solid with 13 mm perforations?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 55.9 cm for the EX stair, against 45.7 cm for the lighter EX-SB.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum thickness must a firewall have?
n: 150 mm, that is 6 inches, extending 300 mm above the roof and 300 mm horizontally.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the maximum opening force for an interior door closer?
n: An interior door closer may not need more than 2.0 kg of opening force. Exterior hinged doors have no set maximum.

q: Under RA 9514, what clearance must a handrail keep from the wall?
n: 38 mm. BP 344 asks for a slightly wider 50 mm.

q: What slope is used for an entryway apron under PD 1096 and PD 957?
n: 1:3 or 1:4, steep because it is short. A ramp anyone must walk up is held to far gentler slopes.

q: Under RA 9514, what horizontal landing dimension applies to a fire exit stair?
n: 60 cm, matching its own 60 cm stair width.

q: What front setback applies to an R-1 lot?
n: R-1, the lowest density, has the deepest front yard at 4.50 m, with 2.00 m sides and rear.

q: What minimum window opening must a bathroom have?
n: 1/20 of the floor area, that is 5%, against 10% for a habitable room.

q: Under PD 1096, a winder must give the full required width of run measured 300 mm from the narrow side. What width is that?
n: The required run is 250 mm, and it must be there 300 mm in from the narrow side. No point on the winder may be narrower than 150 mm.

q: Under BP 220, what is the maximum ramp slope?
n: 15%, roughly 1:6.7, steeper than any accessible ramp. BP 344 governs where wheelchairs must pass.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what minimum tread depth applied to the EX-SB stair, whose treads are flat metal bars?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 15.25 cm, barely a foothold, which is why the type was limited to escape use.

q: What side setback applies to an R-2 lot?
n: 2.00 m on each side, the same as R-1 and R-3.

q: Under RA 9514, what maximum riser height applies to a new stair?
n: 180 mm maximum, 100 mm minimum, paired with a 280 mm tread.

q: What minimum radius must a curved stair have?
n: Not less than the width of the stair itself, so the inner treads stay usable.

q: Under RA 9514, a ramp run must stop for a landing once it climbs how far?
n: 760 mm of rise. The run then needs a landing before it may continue.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what minimum headroom applied to the EX stair, whose treads are solid with 13 mm perforations?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 2.13 m, the most generous of the three: the EX-SB gave 1.98 m and RA 9514 gives 2.00 m.

q: What rear setback applies to an R-3 lot?
n: 2.00 m rear, with 2.00 m sides and a 3.00 m basic front.

q: Under BP 220, what maximum riser height applies to a stair?
n: 250 mm riser with a 200 mm tread, looser than the 200 mm and 250 mm PD 1096 allows.

q: Under BP 344, what minimum clear width must a ramp have?
n: 1.20 m clear, enough for one wheelchair with room to steer.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum height must a main door have?
n: 2000 mm high by 900 mm wide.

q: How high above the floor may a fire exit access opening sit before steps are required?
n: Not over 30.50 cm. Above that height the opening needs steps to reach it.

q: Under PD 957, what minimum access depth and length must connect a subdivision to the main public road?
n: 3.0 m deep by 5.0 m long, the minimum throat between the subdivision and the public road.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what was the maximum height between landings on a Class A stair?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 2.75 m for Class A, against 3.70 m for Class B.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the steepest ramp slope allowed?
n: 1:15 is the steepest allowed, and only in special cases. 1:20 is the standard. The 1994 IRR allowed 1:12.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum width applies to the main door of a socialized housing unit?
n: 800 mm, the same main-door width used across BP 220 housing.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, how many persons per unit could escape by winders or a ladder from an EX-SB balcony?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 38 persons per unit that way, against only 5 through a window.

q: Under PD 1096, what fraction of the road right-of-way sets the minimum sidewalk width?
n: 1/6 of the right-of-way at the low end. Roads under 20.00 m start higher, at 1/4.

q: Under PD 1096, what is the maximum landing length required on a straight stair run?
n: The landing equals the stairway width, but on a straight run it need never exceed 1.20 m.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what capacity did a Class A ramp carry travelling down?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 60 going down against 45 going up, since descent is quicker.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum height applies to a bedroom door?
n: 2000 mm, like every door except bathroom and mezzanine doors.

q: Under BP 344, what minimum handrail height above the floor applies?
n: 700 mm to 900 mm from the floor, the lower rail suiting a seated user.

q: Under BP 344, what minimum sidewalk width must be kept clear?
n: 1.20 m, the same clear width required of a ramp.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what minimum width applied to the EX-SB stair, whose treads are flat metal bars?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 45.7 cm, the narrowest stair the Code allowed, against 55.9 cm for the EX.

q: Under PD 1096, how far must a firewall extend above the roof?
n: 400 mm above the roof, and up to 1000 mm. It also runs 600 mm horizontally past the wall.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what maximum opening force is set for exterior hinged doors?
n: Exterior hinged doors have no set maximum opening force, because wind and door weight vary. Interior door closers are capped at 2.0 kg.

q: Under BP 344, what clearance must a handrail keep from the wall?
n: 50 mm from a wall and 40 mm from a ledge, enough for a full grip.

q: Under PD 1096, what is the maximum slope of an exit court?
n: An exit court may slope up to 1:10, flatter than the 1:8 allowed inside an exit passageway.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what maximum rise applied to the EX stair, whose treads are solid with 13 mm perforations?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 22.9 cm, equal to its 22.9 cm tread. The EX-SB was steeper at 30.5 cm.

q: What side setback applies to an R-1 lot?
n: 2.00 m on each side, with a 4.50 m front and a 2.00 m rear.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum stair width serves an occupant load of 10 or below?
n: 750 mm, allowed only for a private stair. Up to 50 occupants it is 900 mm, above 50 it is 1100 mm.

q: Under RA 9514, what minimum tread depth is allowed at the narrow edge of a winder?
n: 150 mm at the narrow edge, rising to 280 mm measured 305 mm in.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what ramp slope is the standard, used unless the site forces something steeper?
n: 1:20 is the standard. 1:15 is allowed only in special cases. The 1994 IRR allowed 1:12.

q: Under RA 9514, what minimum tread depth applies to a fire exit stair?
n: 23 cm tread with a 23 cm rise.

q: What rear setback applies to an R-2 lot?
n: 2.00 m rear, matching R-1 and R-3.

q: Under RA 9514, what minimum riser height applies to a new stair?
n: 100 mm minimum and 180 mm maximum, so risers cannot be so shallow that users misjudge them.

q: Under RA 9514, what minimum tread depth must a spiral stair provide?
n: 280 mm where it carries egress, with an extra 265 mm of width clear to the outer handrail.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, how was the EX fire exit stair tread constructed?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: Solid, with 13 mm diameter perforations. The EX-SB used flat metal bars instead.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what minimum headroom applied to the EX-SB stair, whose treads are flat metal bars?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 1.98 m, the lowest of the fire exit stair types.

q: Under BP 220, what front setback applies to economic and socialized housing?
n: 1.50 m front and sides, 2.00 m rear.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum tread depth applies to a stair?
n: 200 mm tread with a 250 mm riser. PD 1096 is stricter at 250 mm and 200 mm.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what was the steepest Class A ramp slope?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 1:8, that is 12.5%. Anything steeper fell to Class B.

q: Under RA 9514, what minimum width applies to a main door?
n: 915 mm wide by 2000 mm high, the same 915 mm clear width required of an existing stair.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, how did the EX stair, whose treads are solid with 13 mm perforations discharge to the ground?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: By a swinging stair section only. The lighter EX-SB could also use a ladder.

q: What clearance applies between buildings of 1 to 2 storeys?
n: 4.0 m between buildings and 1.50 m to the property line, the tightest band.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what was the maximum height between landings on a Class B stair?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 3.70 m for Class B, against 2.75 m for Class A.

q: Under RA 9514, what maximum cross slope applies to a ramp?
n: 1:48 across the run, so a wheelchair does not drift sideways while climbing.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum height applies to the main door of a socialized housing unit?
n: 2000 mm, with an 800 mm minimum width.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, how many persons per unit could escape through an EX-SB balcony door?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 45 persons per unit through the balcony door, the same figure RA 9514 uses for a door today.

q: Under PD 1096, how is the required sidewalk width set for a road right-of-way of 30.00 m and above?
o: From 1/6 up to 1/4 of the RROW width
From 1/4 up to 1/3 of the RROW width
n: PD 1096 sets sidewalks as a fraction of the road right-of-way, not a fixed width. Wide roads of 30.00 m and up give 1/6 to 1/4; narrow roads below 20.00 m give 1/4 to 1/3, so a small road gives up more of itself to the sidewalk.

q: Under RA 9514, what minimum landing dimension applies along a ramp?
n: 1120 mm, the same figure as the minimum ramp width, so the landing never pinches the run.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what capacity did a Class B ramp carry travelling down?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 45 either way for Class B, unlike Class A which rose to 60 going down.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum width applies to a bathroom door?
n: 600 mm, the narrowest door BP 220 allows.

q: Under BP 344, what maximum handrail height above the tread surface applies?
n: 1200 mm at most above the tread. The minimum sits at 700 mm to 900 mm from the floor.

q: Under PD 1096, what planting strip widths bracket the range within a road right-of-way?
n: 0.20 m at least, for grass and shrubs, up to 1.20 m on a right-of-way of 30.00 m and above. Trees need 0.30 m.
